reason: Equivalent, measured by the mutation run itself: the mutant runs every LESS verify of the LESS known answers and the wrapper tests on an 8 MiB thread, and the gate accepts this ledger entry only if that run ends as survived (no crash, no failure). Expected from the frames: LESS_verify's largest locals are Gs[8] generator matrices of 126 x 256 bytes (256 KiB), near the 0.4 MB the header documents, and pthread_attr_setstacksize accepts 8 MiB.

Equivalent for every input: when pthread_attr_init fails no thread is created, so run_open never writes j.rc, which keeps its initial -1 (the job initializer); the open expression then gives valid = 1 && (-1 == 0) = 0, the same 0 as the original. (glibc's pthread_attr_init also never fails.)

Equivalent for every input: ok is 0 only when setstacksize failed (pthread_create then not called, short-circuit) or pthread_create failed; in both cases no thread ran, j.rc keeps its initial -1 (the job initializer) and the open expression gives valid = 1 && (-1 == 0) = 0, the same as the original.

Equivalent for every input: the mutant still joins (it only ignores the result). pthread_join fails only with EDEADLK (joining itself or a join cycle), EINVAL (thread not joinable or already being joined) or ESRCH (no such thread); t was created joinable by this call (default attr), is joined exactly once here by its creator, so none can occur and the result is always 0, i.e. the original returns 1 too.

Equivalent for every input: size_t arithmetic is modulo 2^64, and 2^64 and SIG_MAX - SIG_MIN = 176 are both multiples of 16, so (SIG_MIN - sig_len) and (SIG_MAX - sig_len) are congruent mod 16 for every sig_len (including sig_len > SIG_MIN, where the subtraction wraps); the % 16 test gives the same answer.

Equivalent for every input: the guard differs only when msg_len == 0, where the mutant calls memcpy(sm, msg, 0) with msg NULL; a zero-length memcpy copies nothing and glibc reads no source byte, so sm is unchanged. (The guard exists for C-standard hygiene, not behaviour.)

Equivalent for every input: j.rc is read (the open expression) only after on_big_stack(run_open, ..) returned nonzero, which on POSIX requires pthread_create == 0 and pthread_join == 0, i.e. open_thread ran run_open to completion and assigned j.rc = crypto_sign_open(...) (run_open), overwriting the initial value.

When the memcmp line is evaluated, j.rc == 0 and j.mlen == msg_len (the open expression short-circuits otherwise). crypto_sign_open then did *mlen = smlen - sig_len and memcpy(m, sm, *mlen) (lib/sign.c:106-107) before LESS_verify, which only reads m; sm[0..msg_len) is msg (the copy above). So m[0..msg_len) == msg and memcmp(m, msg, msg_len) == 0 for every such input; for msg_len == 0 it is memcmp(m, NULL, 0), which compares nothing and returns 0 in glibc. Replacing the comparison with 1 gives the same value. The copy is lib/sign.c:106-107: `*mlen = smlen - (unsigned long long)sig_len;` then `memcpy((unsigned char *) m, (const unsigned char *) sm, (size_t) *mlen);`, and LESS_verify receives m as `const char *const`. Caveat: with an empty message a caller may pass msg = NULL, and memcmp(m, NULL, 0) is undefined behaviour in ISO C before C2y; glibc compares nothing and returns 0, and this gate runs on glibc only.

Equivalent: at msg_len == SIZE_MAX - sizeof(sign_t) - 16 the original continues with cap == SIZE_MAX, and allocating SIZE_MAX bytes fails on every allocator (no address space holds it), so sm is NULL, ok stays 0 and the function returns 0, the same result as the early return of the mutant.

Equivalent for every input: the two conditions differ only when j.smlen == msg_len, where the original computes j.smlen - msg_len = 0 and the mutant takes the else branch, also 0. n is the same in every case.

Equivalent for every input: crypto_sign (lib/sign.c) writes msg into sm, has LESS_sign write the signature as a sign_t at sm + mlen, and returns 0 with *smlen = mlen + LESS_SIGNATURE_SIZE(k), where k is LESS_sign's result: the GGMPath count of published seed-tree nodes, or 0 on its pivot-failure return. The challenge has exactly W = 34 non-zero entries of T = 45, so 11 leaves are revealed and every published node covers a distinct non-empty set of them: 0 <= k <= 11 = MAX_PUBLISHED_SEEDS. So n = smlen - msg_len = SIG_MIN + 16k with SIG_MIN <= n <= SIG_MAX, and sizeof(sign_t) (packed: 2 digests, W monomial actions, MAX_PUBLISHED_SEEDS seeds + 1) equals LESS_SIGNATURE_SIZE(MAX_PUBLISHED_SEEDS) = SIG_MAX. Hence j.smlen = msg_len + n <= msg_len + SIG_MAX < msg_len + sizeof(sign_t) + 16 = cap, so the dropped test is always true.

So n = smlen - msg_len = SIG_MIN + 16k with SIG_MIN <= n <= SIG_MAX, and sizeof(sign_t) (packed: 2 digests, W monomial actions, MAX_PUBLISHED_SEEDS seeds + 1) equals LESS_SIGNATURE_SIZE(MAX_PUBLISHED_SEEDS) = SIG_MAX. Every byte the reference writes lies in sm[0, msg_len + sizeof(sign_t)): the message copy, the sign_t fields (salt, digest, seed_storage cleared over its own SEED_TREE_MAX_PUBLISHED_BYTES and filled with at most 11 seeds, cf_monom_actions[0..W)) and the trailing count byte sm[mlen + n - 1] with n <= SIG_MAX. So the 16 bytes of slack are never written, and with cap = msg_len + sizeof(sign_t) the later test j.smlen <= cap still holds (j.smlen <= msg_len + SIG_MAX). Same writes, same result.

Equivalent for every input: the mutant differs only when msg == NULL, which the argument check admits only with msg_len == 0. The reference then reads the message twice, both with length 0: memcpy(sm, m, 0) in crypto_sign copies nothing, and LESS_SHA3_INC_ABSORB(&state, m, 0) is keccak_inc_absorb, whose loop needs mlen + s_inc[25] >= r (false: s_inc[25] < r after every absorb) and whose KeccakF1600_StateXORBytes(.., m, .., 0) loops over i < 0. No byte of m is read, so NULL and &none give the same digest and signature.
